note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Moses chose “rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” What is the sin he refused? John defines it: “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Sin is breaking God’s law. The pleasures of sin are the pleasures of transgressing the law, and if anybody says sin isn’t pleasurable, that’s a lie. It is very fun. But you have to perform abstinence, and choose affliction with the people of God over it, the way Moses did.

That is the difference between Moses and the hireling. A hireling has a temporary time in this truth. He or she doesn’t care about salvation, and is willing to destroy the family, the brotherhood, everything they built up, just for their own sin. The love of sin. The hireling chooses the pleasure of transgressing the law for a season; the true servant chooses to suffer with the people of God.

precepts.text: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one: Cain was Satan's baby, spiritually obviously. John is saying what Christ said in John 8:44. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous. And he killed Abel savagely, by the way. It wasn't like he just cut his throat. It was very bad. I'mma show you how.
precepts.point: And abode not in the truth: remember, in process of time he would offer up fruit. What was he supposed to offer up? Animals. So he abode not in the truth. It's not talking about Satan; Satan was always a liar, that's his job; he's called the devil, which means liar. It's talking about Cain. Remember what Cain said to the Lord: I don't know. Was he lying? Yes. He is a liar and the father of it.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Christ said to his own people, “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning”. Those same Jews wanted Christ dead; they were plotting to kill him. Did Satan murder anybody? No. Who killed in the beginning? Cain. Christ is calling him the devil. The Lord said to Cain he would hide his face from him, and Cain's father became the devil.

John says what Christ said in John 8:44: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was Satan's baby, spiritually obviously. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” And he killed Abel savagely; it wasn't like he just cut his throat, it was very bad.

So “the lusts of your father ye will do” means the same way Cain killed his brother, you are going to kill me: the same spirit that was in Cain is in you. “and abode not in the truth”: in process of time Cain offered up fruit, when he was supposed to offer up animals. It is not talking about Satan, who was always a liar; that's his job. It's talking about Cain. When the Lord asked for his brother, Cain said I don't know. Was he lying? Yes: “he is a liar, and the father of it.”

The commentaries on Genesis 4:7 all tap dance around this and don't want to be honest about it. Be very careful about modern scholarship, because they hide things; older scholars are more upfront, and there is a movement set up to censor any biblical truth that can be substantiated.

precepts.text: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. That is Simon. The domino effect: he coveted power, from there it turned to anger, from there to slander, and from there to murder. Holding on to anger is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die; the only one affected is you.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.”

That is Simon. He hated Onias, his brother, and his faction committed murders. This is the domino effect: it starts off as coveting; Simon coveted power. From there it turned to anger, from there to slander, and from there to murder. It is never just one sin, and not only are you affected, the people you sinned against are affected too.

Holding on to anger is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die. You are drinking poison waiting for somebody else to drop dead, and they are not dropping dead. The only one being affected is you. This goes for men and women.

Onias was the opposite. He went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private”. He did not even go there to accuse Simon. That is the difference between a brother and a betrayer.

precepts.text: Behold what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God. This is the New Testament talking. Therefore the world knoweth us not: they call us Negroes and refuse to believe these are the people of the book, because it knew him not; to this day they refuse to say Christ was a black man of the tribe of Judah.
precepts.point: After the Most High sent the flood, those same spirits came right back through the three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Genesis 5 traces the lineage from Adam down to Noah, who “begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Then Genesis 6 says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair.” The sons of God are that lineage just named; the daughters of men are the daughters of the other nations that were created. These are not literal angels. The chapter before gives the understanding, and the scriptures that follow prove who the sons of God are.

John writes it in the New Testament: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.” That is what God calls us. Brothers, you are walking gods, whoever gets upset about it, the apologists included.

“therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” The world looks at our people, calls us Negroes, and refuses to believe these could be the people of the book, the sons of God. And it knew him not: to this day they refuse to say Christ was a black man. They put the image of Cesare Borgia in every church, comic book and piece of media, while the Bible says he is black, of the tribe of Judah.

So when Genesis 6 speaks of “the sons of God” going in to the daughters of men, it is speaking of the same people John calls the sons of God: Adam’s line, our forefathers.

precepts.text: When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul: you will have brothers and sisters say the wicked are going to be destroyed, and meanwhile you are moving in the same spirit. You curse Satan and curse your own soul, because when you become overcome with it you take on the same attributes Cain did. We have to exercise ourselves to have a conscience void of offense, and deal with our brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God; do not let it fester and resonate in your spirit.
precepts.point: He that loveth not his brother abideth in death: that brother's home is death. Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
John says “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Even the scribes and Pharisees took on the spirit of Cain, of Satan; they moved in the same exact spirit, bitter toward Christ and wanting to put him to death. That spirit will jump on us too, and we have to deal with it. When we are overcome with it, we take on the same attributes Cain did.

“When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” You will have brothers and sisters say, the white man is the devil, they're going to be destroyed, they're going into captivity. And meanwhile you are moving in the same spirit. So you curse Satan, and you curse your own soul, because you have hatred toward your brother. Brothers talk bold against the white man and find themselves in the same spirit as him.

“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.” Whoever is bitter toward his brother is in the spirit of Cain; you are in the same spirit. That hatred is always masked: “Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” He acted like his friend to get him in position.

So we have to exercise ourselves to have a conscience void of offence. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God. Don't allow it to fester and resonate in your spirit until you are overcome, because “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren.”

For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil: so why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think we are moving in the spirit of Christ? In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. precepts.point: For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears: hold on to that bitter spirit and you will find that same place of no repentance. In that day it will be too late; the judgment is set.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Hebrews warns of the “root of bitterness springing up”, and John shows what spirit jumps on you when you move that way. “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” That is the history being drawn out from Cain to Esau: the devil sinned from the beginning, and the same spirit runs down through his children.

“For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.” The purpose of Christ is to destroy the works of the devil. So why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think that we are moving in the spirit of Christ?

“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God.” This is the manifestation of the children of God. If you don't do righteousness, you are not of God. The scripture tells us how to deal uprightly with our brother and sister: if there is an offense, go by Matthew 18:15. You don't sow discord and murmur in the midst of the congregation and spread that spirit through our brothers and sisters.

“neither he that loveth not his brother.” When you don't love your brother, you are not moving in the spirit of Christ and you are not counted a child of God. You are the son and daughter of Cain, of Esau. We have to be mindful of this spirit and purge that leaven, that bitter spirit, out of us.

precepts.text: In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil. John was telling the Israelites he wrote to: love one another, not as Cain, who was of that wicked one. Cain was under Satan; Satan was his father. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.
precepts.point: If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. They did not just kill the one man that hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage. That is how Esau gets down; remember who their desire was to.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
In case anyone doubts that Satan ruled over Cain, John explains it: “In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.” There are children of God on the earth, and there are children of the devil.

John was correcting the Israelites he wrote to: “For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.” “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” He was telling them, do not be like Cain. And who is that wicked one? The devil of verse 10. Cain was under Satan; Satan was his father.

“And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” That is Genesis 4: Abel did well and was accepted, Cain did not do well, his desire went to Satan, and “Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.”

It shows in Cain's seed. Lamech said, “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.” “If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” They did not just kill the one man who hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage: the sons, the daughters, the aunts, the grandparents. That is how Esau gets down too. Remember who their desire was to: Satan. Everybody comes from Adam, but not everybody is a child of God.

precepts.text: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God. The sons of God is not talking about angels coming down.
precepts.point: The earth was filled with violence through them: that them goes back to Cain's seed. Cain's seed was influencing everybody; what we read in Genesis 4 about Cain's children affected all people on the earth. So God told Noah, Make thee an ark of gopher wood.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
All of this was happening in the city called Enoch, named after Cain's son. Genesis says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” In Christianity they say the sons of God are angels coming down. John shows who the sons of God are: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”.

The sons of God is not talking about angels. It is talking about men, our people. Before we were called Israelites, we were called the sons of God.

Genesis 6 proves it: “And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh”. God is angry with man, the sons of God, who are flesh, not angels. It is hard to see how Christian scholars can read that and say angels.

So when the sons of God took them wives of all which they chose, it is talking about interracial marriage: we started marrying the women of other nations. It still happens, a brother bringing in a white woman and claiming she is of the tribe of Gad, when everybody knows she is an Edomite.

precepts.text: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother, because his own works were evil and his brother's righteous. Cain was the seed of the devil.
precepts.point: Cain rose up and slew Abel. That is the fulfilment of Genesis 3:15 and the first blood shed in the war: Cain, Satan's seed, killed our forefather.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
Genesis 4 shows Satan’s children being born in the earth. Eve bare Cain and then Abel; Abel kept sheep and Cain tilled the ground. “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth”. The Lord told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” Do good and you will be accepted; do evil and Satan will rule over you. Cain would become the child of Satan and serve him.

Then Cain talked with Abel, “and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him”. That is the fulfillment of Genesis 3:15, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. The enmity started there. Cain, Satan’s seed, killed our forefather: the first murder on the earth and the first blood shed in the war.

John proves Cain was that seed: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” Cain was always evil. His descendants were the children of the devil, and they corrupted everyone on the earth, even the sons of God, until God destroyed the world. All the evil you see Esau doing on the earth today, Cain was doing back then.

Then the sons of God and the sons of the devil came back. Rebekah’s children “struggled together within her”, and the Lord said, “Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”. Jacob is the twelve tribes, the so-called Negroes and Hispanics; Esau is the so-called white man. This fight did not start with slavery, Jim Crow or civil rights; it started in the beginning with Cain and Abel, and was reborn as Jacob and Esau: good against evil. Many of our people followed Cain then, and many follow Esau now and have become children of the devil themselves.

Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, born without pigment, as Cain lost his when the earth cursed him. Jacob took hold on his heel, a prophetic sign of Genesis 3:15: our Lord coming to destroy Satan and his children. And when scripture says “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, it was Herod, an Edomite, who “killed James the brother of John with the sword” and took Peter. The devil means the deceiver, and it is interchangeable: the father and his children, who can do nothing without the father that dwells in them.

precepts.text: In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil. Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.
precepts.point: Cain's line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil”. There are children of God on the planet, and there are children of the devil on the planet. And “whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another”.

“Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Wait: we thought Cain was of Adam. It says no. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of that wicked one, of Satan. That is exactly what God told Cain in Genesis 4: unto thee shall be his desire, and he shall rule over thee. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.”

This is the enmity of Genesis 3:15 made plain: “between thy seed and her seed”. Satan’s seed is Cain, the children of the devil, and her seed is Israel, the children of God.

Cain’s line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob. Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Idumea, the Greek and Roman name for Edom, is that same Esau. So when we ask who the children of the devil are in the earth today and why they hate us, John has already told us: not as Cain, who was of that wicked one.

precepts.text: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. Before the physical act comes the thought, and God counts the thought as breaking thou shalt not kill.
precepts.point: If your head is full of evil, maybe you are not reading enough. The brothers who do not know the scriptures are the ones who will betray you and plant things in your house. Young men, when did you and the brother you talk to all week last discuss scripture?

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

precepts.why:
Christ lists what comes out of the heart of men, and murders is among them: “evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.” Some do not understand how murder can come out of the mind, so John makes it plain: “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.”

The hatred you carry is equivalent to murder. Where does it all begin? In your mind, as Mark 7 says. Before you ever commit the act of physical murder, it has to begin with a thought, and the thought of it is the exact same thing. The hatred we have as a people one for another: God says you're already a murderer. You already broke the commandment thou shalt not kill.

It works the same with adultery. The minute you see that ex at the grocery store and take his phone number, before you have even said anything, that is adultery right there. It starts in the mind.

Nobody knows you more than Messiah. He created you, so he knows what is in your mind. We cannot read your mind, but he can, and “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” So deal with the hatred while it is still a thought, because no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.

precepts.text: Sin is the transgression of the law.
precepts.point: Keep my commandments and live. Whoever does not keep the law will not live.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
If the law is holy and just and good, then what is it to break it? “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

The law of the beasts in Leviticus 11 was given “to make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” Some animals are clean and some are unclean; it is basic. So eating the unclean, pork, lobster, shrimp, oysters, snails (escargot is just French for snails), crabs, chitlins, pig feet, is transgressing the law, and transgressing the law is sin.

Overeating is sin too. Brothers who are strong in many areas, who left the porn, the smoking and the stealing when they came to the truth, still cannot say, I am not going to overeat any more. There is one area kicking their butt, to the point where they will lie about it: drinking from the brother’s slurpee on the way back from the store, eating the whole house’s bread and saying nah with the crumbs all over the bed. Where there is one sin there are many more; a demon does not walk by itself.

So keeping the holy law means keeping all of it. Gluttony and unclean food are not small things outside the commandments; they are the transgression of the law, and that is sin.

precepts.text: We are called the sons of God.
precepts.point: Their children turned into giants and wickedness, and man's days were cut to 120 years.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
After Exodus 4:22, 1 John 3:1 confirms it: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”. We who? We Israelites. The sons of God of Genesis 6 are not angels; they are us.

So Genesis 6 is about our fathers: “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” Our sons became famous men. “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” The man God was angry with was the sons of God. Once we broke the laws we already had and went in unto the daughters of men, our kids turned into the devil and started acting like the devil on the planet. That is why God had to bring the flood.

Psalm 82:6-7 says of us: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High. But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” The flood came and we all died, and we came back through Noah's son Shem. And we still have not learned our lesson. Today the same snares catch our men and women who leave their own people for other nations, and it costs them everything.

precepts.text: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer, and no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.
precepts.point: Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. Inner hatred, given room, plots death; that is why the law says thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart.

note.label: Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer

precepts.why:
“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.” The brethren had not yet laid a hand on Joseph when they saw him afar off, but in their hearts they had already killed him: “Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit.” Inner hatred, given room, plots death.

That is why the law says thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart. The hatred was there first, and the conspiring to slay him came out of it. It is the same spirit Cain had, and the same spirit Esau had: “Behold, this dreamer cometh.”

And no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him. The hating of a brother is not a small thing; it is murder in the sight of God, and it costs a man eternal life.

precepts.point: And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” The sin being forgiven, “forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin”, is the breaking of the law given to Israel.

The word and the statutes were given to Israel only, so this mercy is spoken to Israel. And it does not clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged, “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.”

precepts.text: The spirit of anger and hatred transitions to murder; whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.
precepts.point: Not everything is a Matthew 18: Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend, because many times what you heard is just a tale.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
